_comment: Copy to job.json (gitignored) and edit. Run it with:
hosts   - the machines to drive, and the ONE login for each
actions - what to do, in order, on every host
This file holds plaintext passwords. It is gitignored. Treat it like a
password file and keep it off shared drives.
_hosts_comment: One login per endpoint. Each host's login does BOTH jobs:
opening the session - the SERVER hands it to Windows Credential Manager
so mstsc authenticates. The model never sees it and
signing in inside   - the model fills a sign-in box (Outlook, a portal)
and this host substitutes the real value at the
keyboard. It really is typed into the app; it never
enters the model's context, the console, or the
"login" always means the account for the machine currently being driven.
While working on one host, no other host's password exists in the model's
world at all - so it cannot be typed on the wrong machine.
Passwords must be typeable on the REMOTE keyboard layout. Accented or
non-Latin characters cannot be sent over RDP - the run reports that the
login could not be typed rather than half-typing it.
_actions_comment: A plain string is an action that may type the host's login if it needs to.
Use "secrets": [] on every step that does not sign in. A step that never
needs the password should not be able to type it - that is the main guard
against a model being talked into typing it somewhere it should not.
Write each action the way you would brief a new person: one concrete
outcome, naming what they should see when it is done. Vague goals fail.

actions.do: Open Outlook. If it asks for a password, use the saved login. Stop when the inbox is on screen.
